Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 through § 2-2033. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
NOTICE OF MEETING 
 
Notice is hereby given that a meeting of the Salem Conservation Commission will be held on October 22, 2026, 
at 6:30 p.m. via remote participation in accordance with Chapter 2 of the Act of 2025.  
 
 
MEETING MINUTES 
 
 
The meeting was opened at 6:30 pm. 
 
I. ROLL CALL  
• In attendance: Emmet Costen, Lucia DelNegro, Graeme Marcoux, Dayton Marchese, Dan Ricciarelli, and 
Bart Hoskins 
 
City Staff: Rachel Vresilovic 
 
II.     OLD | NEW BUSINESS 
 
1. 115 Swampscott Rd- legal review update 
• Robin Stein with KP Law was present to discuss this item. She provided the Commission with a 
confidential memo if it isn’t discussed in a public meeting.  
• She noted that the Conservation Restriction isn’t the easiest to interpret.  
• The Commission could go into Executive Session if they are looking to litigate.  
• Mr. Hoskins noted that the Commission has received the memo with legal opinions and Ms. 
Vresilovic’s memo summarizing where things stand.  
• Mr. Hoskins noted that there are two sections of the property under lease agreement and when the 
CR went into effect, it was intended to exclude those lease agreements. The question is whether 
the exclusions go beyond the life of the lease agreements.  
• Ms. Stein said she wasn’t sure if the Commission had concerns with the CR but knows they have 
heard complaints from residents.  
• Mr. Hoskins asked if the leases were still in effect. Ms. Stein said that since the time the CR was 
recorded, one of the lease holders has become the landowner. She believes there are questions on 
interpretation.  
• Mr. Hoskins said the property owner still needs to follow the Wetlands Protection Act. He noted 
that an agreement or statement may be needed so that the Commission can go back and note that 
something new has happened on the property that does not comport with the CR.  
• Mr. Ricciarelli noted that there may be a sublease that is clearing the site and erecting buildings, 
which was not in the original spirit of the CR. He asked whether they knew where the property lines 
are or where their jurisdiction lies.  
• Mr. Hoskins said there seems to be ambiguity of the lease area and the CR exempted the lease area.  
 
CITY OF SALEM 
CONSERVATION COMMISSION
City of Salem Conservation Commission 
Draft Minutes for October 22, 2026 
Page 2 of 10 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028  
through § 2-2033. 
 
• Ms. DelNegro said she thought an enforcement order was issued months ago and that one of the 
action items was to submit a survey plan showing the Commission’s jurisdiction. She inquired about 
what permits were secured.  
• Ms. Vresilovic said the owner installed erosion controls and that her understanding was that no 
enforcement order was given as the Commission was working to determine the CR issue.  
• Ms. DelNegro said this was one of the first issues residents reached out to her about when she 
joined the Commission. Mr. Ricciarelli said he thought they first needed to find out what their 
jurisdiction was on the property before issuing an enforcement order.  
• Ms. DelNegro said she recalls asking for a survey plan showing all the alterations, resources, and 
buffer zones. She asked if Ms. Vresilovic could go back and check to see what orders may have been 
voted on.  
• Mr. Hoskins said there were two different tracks – CR violations and wetland violation issues. He 
does recall discussing needing a survey showing the resources and buildings. He wasn’t sure 
whether that was something the Commission could request of the owner, or whether the 
Commission would have had to do that.  
• Mr. Ricciarelli said it’s usually up to the applicant to prove something isn’t jurisdictional. Mr. 
Hoskins agreed that the need for the jurisdictional lines is important.  
• Mr. Hoskins said there still seems to be ambiguity about what the CR permits. 
• Ms. Vresilovic noted that she found the wetland delineations that were completed last year, and 
that the delineations are in the project folder.  
• Ms. DelNegro noted that she believes the item should remain on the agenda.  
• The CR was recorded in 1980. It does not expire as it was approved by the Commonwealth.  
• Mr. Marchese suggested that the Commission come up with a list of issues they see with the CR and 
then meet with the property owner to discuss and find middle ground. Mr. Hoskins said that may be 
the best path forward.  
• Ms. DelNegro noted the concern of the residents such as the building, lack of access, and roadway 
that has taken place on the CR and may have also taken place within the wetland.  
• Mr. Hoskins said now that they have the wetland delineation, they can act on that information.  
• Ms. DelNegro requested a site visit be set up. Ms. Vresilovic said she could coordinate that visit.  
• Brian Leclair, attorney for the property owner, was present. He noted that they have been trying to 
cooperate.  
• Mr. Leclair noted that a problem with the CR is that rights impacting the lease holder should not 
have been granted as the owner did not have the power to grant them. He will submit information 
on the case law on this issue. He does not feel there is ambiguity in the CR.  
• Mr. Leclair said the fence was installed at the request of the Police Department over 20 years ago. 
He said the statute of limitations has passed. He said he doesn’t believe the Building Department 
permitting issues fall under the jurisdiction of the Conservation Commission.  
• The wetland delineation showing fence location and building location was shared.  
• Ms. DelNegro again said she was concerned about the apparent expanded earth work that has 
more recently happened.  
• Mr. Marcoux said that based on aerial imagery, there has been significant work happening on the 
property. He noted the fence line hasn’t changed, but the activity within the fence line certainly has 
changed. Mr. Leclair said the appearance of change may be due to seasonal differences when the 
aerials were taken.
City of Salem Conservation Commission 
Draft Minutes for October 22, 2026 
Page 3 of 10 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028  
through § 2-2033. 
 
• Ms. Vresilovic said she would share the historic aerial imagery with the Commission and will 
coordinate with the property owner to schedule a site visit with the Commission.  
• Ms. DelNegro said she really needs to see the property.  
• Mr. Hoskins said he believes it’s up to the City, with legal counsel, not the Commission, to decide on 
what they can enforce on the CR.  
• Ms. Stein said they can keep the item on the agenda but aren’t required to as it is not a public 
hearing.  
• Mr. Leclair said it would take him two weeks before he can send the appropriate legal materials to 
town counsel. Ms. Vresilovic asked if Mr. Leclair could also send her the documents, and he said he 
would.  
 
 
III. REGULAR AGENDA  
 
A. 54-56 Margin Street, 5 High Street, 20-24 Endicott Street #64-832 – Continuance of Public Hearing - 
Notice of Intent for Harborlight Homes, for a redevelopment of multiple parcels into affordable housing 
and shelter beds with service. The site is located at 54-56 Margin Street, 7 High Street & 20-24 
Endicott Street (Map 25, Lots 595 & 597) within an area subject to protection under the Wetlands 
Protection Act MGL c.131§40 and Salem Wetlands Protection and Conservation Ordinance.  
 
Pat Connolly, project manager, for Harborlight was present to discuss the project.  
• Ms. Vresilovic noted that the project is still undergoing peer review with the Planning Board for stormwater 
management and drainage. 
• Mr. Connolly reported that they just received comments back from the peer reviewer today, which he 
shared with Ms. Vresilovic.  
• Mr. Connolly said the City Engineer is satisfied with the review and that any remaining issues need to be 
addressed prior to issuance of a Building Permit.  
• Mr. Ricciarelli said he would be comfortable issuing an order of conditions since the wetland impact is so 
small.  
• If there are changes to the stormwater plan it would need to come back to the Commission for an 
amendment.  
• Mr. Marchese noted that his questions at the last meeting were around the stormwater management and if 
they are being covered he does not have any objections.  
• Ms. DelNegro expressed concern about the Commission’s agent not receiving a copy of the peer review 
sooner.  
• Ms. Vresilovic said the City Engineer did not specifically review the wetland impacts and that there will be 
other conditions to the project from the Planning Board.  
• There would be a quorum if Ms. DelNegro voted present.  
• Mr. Hoskins noted that if it is likely there will be changes, then it may make sense to wait to approve.  
• Mr. Connolly said if they can come before the Commission at their next meeting, it would not impact their 
schedule.  
• Ms. Vresilovic said she would coordinate with the applicant to make sure the Commission had all the 
necessary materials for their November meeting.  
  
A motion to continue the hearing was made by Dan Ricciarelli, seconded by Graeme Marcoux, and passes 6-0.
City of Salem Conservation Commission 
Draft Minutes for October 22, 2026 
Page 4 of 10 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028  
through § 2-2033. 
 
B. Restaurant Row #64-834- Public Hearing- Notice of Intent for the City of Salem, for pedestrian 
connection improvements located between Salem Willows Parking Area and Dead Horse Beach. The 
improvements include a new sidewalk with accessible curb ramps, and markings. The site is located 
between Salem Willows Park and Dead Horse Beach (Map 45, Lot 89) within an area subject to protection 
under the Wetlands Protection Act MGL c.131§40 and Salem Wetlands Protection and Conservation 
Ordinance.  
 
Stephanie MacDonald was present to discuss the proposal: 
• A plan showing the wetland resource areas was shared.  
• The project will improve the safety of the sidewalk. The sidewalk would be 6’ wide and will include full 
ADA accessibility. 
• The project falls within Land Subject to Coastal Zone Flowage and FEMA E Zone. 
• The project proposes milling over the existing roadway and a new curb. Concrete would be used for the 
sidewalk.  
• Part of the project is a redevelopment.  
• Most of the disturbance within the buffer are temporary and permanent impacts are small, less than 5’, 
and consist primarily of grading. 
• No new drainage features are proposed, and no new discharges are created. Control barriers are 
proposed.  
• Images of the area were shared.  
• Mr. Marcoux noted the dangerousness of the area. 
• Ms. DelNegro noted it was a great presentation and acknowledged the strong need for the project.  
• The curve in the proposed sidewalk is due to the grade change.  
 
The meeting was open for public comment. There were no comments or questions.  
 
A motion to close the public hearing was made by Dan Ricciarelli, seconded by Graeme Marcoux, and passes 6-0. 
 
A motion to issue a standard Order of Conditions was made by Dan Riccarelli, seconded by Dayton Marchese, 
and passes 6-0. 
 
C. 17 March St Ct - #64-835 – Public Hearing- Notice of Intent for Steven Donovan and Abbey Noone for the 
proposed construction of two additions and a deck to a single-family dwelling. The site is located at 17 
March St Ct (Map 37, Lot 16) within an area subject to protection under the Wetlands Protection Act MGL 
c.131§40 and Salem Wetlands Protection and Conservation Ordinance.  
 
Nicole Ferrara, LEC Environmental, was present to discuss the proposal: 
• Ms. Ferrara shared and reviewed an aerial and site plan of the property.  
• There is an existing shed, patio, decking, and retaining wall on the property.  
• The resource areas were determined in 2024 and include coastal bank, buffer zone, river front, and land 
subject to coastal zone flowage.   
• DEP commented that there wasn’t any topography shown on the plan, and LiDAR were provided that 
showed the retaining wall is the bank boundary.  
• Proposed construction would take place within the existing building footprint and lawn area.
City of Salem Conservation Commission 
Draft Minutes for October 22, 2026 
Page 5 of 10 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028  
through § 2-2033. 
 
• The proposed entryway is within the footprint of driveway and lawn. The second story deck would 
come out front the second story addition.  
• A portion of the paver patio would be removed.  
• Any new surfaces are in previously degraded areas. 
• The applicant is proposing erosion controls, and riverfront area mitigation restoration plan with 
plantings. Two areas totaling 400SF are proposed to be restored.  
• The plan list and landscape plan was shared.  
• DEP commented on the erosion control boundary and a revised plan was provided that avoided the 
mitigation area.  
• Mr. Ricciarelli noted that he did not believe there would be many impacts since it was second story 
addition. He inquired about where construction materials would be stored. Ms. Ferrara said they would 
be placed within the existing driveway. 
• Ms. DelNegro said she liked the restoration plan and recommended a condition that a full or partial 
certificate not be issued until the restoration planting was complete and that the Commission consider 
language requiring a certain success rate within two years.  
• Mr. Marcoux noted that there seems to be a net loss of impervious surface. Ms. Ferrara said the 
restoration was intended to improve the riverfront area as a demonstrated improvement. Mr. Marcoux 
said he would support requiring planting success after two years.  
• Ms. Ferrara said the list of plants came from the list of native coastal plants and homeowner’s 
recommendation.  
• Ms. DelNegro recommended a partial Certificate not be issued until the area is planted and then a full 
certificate be issued two years after to ensure the plantings survived.  
• The homeowners are long-term owners.  
• The plan includes planting a minimum of two trees and eight shrubs.  
 
The meeting was open for public comment. There were no comments or questions.  
 
A motion to close the public hearing was made by Dayton Marchese, seconded by Dan Ricciarelli, and passes 6-0. 
 
A motion to issue a standard Order of Conditions with a special condition that a partial certificate not be issued 
until the plantings are in place and that full certificate not be issued until two growing seasons have passed with 
photos showing a 75% survival rate was made by Dan Riccarelli, seconded by Lucia DelNegro, and passes 6-0. 
 
 
D. 0 Waite St - #64-836- Public Hearing – Notice of Intent for James Rynes, Massachusetts Electric 
Company, for proposed underground cable removal work. The site is located at 0 Waite St (Map 36, Lot 
234) within an area subject to protection under the Wetlands Protection Act MGL c.131§40 and Salem 
Wetlands Protection and Conservation Ordinance.  
 
Kasey Pearl and Honora Lovelace, BSC Group, was present to discuss the proposal: 
• The environmental resources map was shared and reviewed. 
• Wetland resources impacted include BVW, land subject to coastal zone flowage, and the 100 ft buffer 
zone to BVW.  
• Construction matting within the BVW will be used.
City of Salem Conservation Commission 
Draft Minutes for October 22, 2026 
Page 6 of 10 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028  
through § 2-2033. 
 
• A trench is proposed to be dug to access the cables, and excavated material will be stockpiled next to 
the trench and replaced once the cables have been removed.  
• Nineteen trees will need to removed and given the nature of the site are not proposed to be replaced.  
• The applicant is requesting a waiver of the 2:1 mitigation ratio.  
• Woody regrowth is proposed. 
• BMPs will be used to access the site.  
• It is unclear as to why there are two DEP numbers assigned to the project as there is only one file.  
• The matting requires the trees to be removed.  
• Ms. DelNegro recommended the applicant reach out to DEP to clarify the file number question.  
• The proposal is to use the least amount of matting and impact to complete the project.  
• Once the cable is removed, the area is proposed to revegetate naturally. 
• Ms. DelNegro said it appears the work is temporary and necessary for safety. Ms. Pearl said the cables 
have reached the end of their useful life.  
• Mr. Marcoux noted that many of the trees are already dead.  
• Photos of the area were shared.  
• Mr. Hoskins inquired if any thought had been given to addressing the phragmites. He noted the 
disturbed soil could lead to more phragmites. Mr. Hoskins suggested that a condition could be to 
require phragmites control after one year. Ms. Pearl thought they may be able to do that work by hand.   
• Ms. Honora noted that a wetland seed mix could be used, but that going back in could cause additional 
disturbance. Mr. Hoskins said he thought the phragmites could be pulled by hand. Ms. Honora said the 
area is already impacted by phragmites. Mr. Hoskins withdrew his suggestion. 
 
The meeting was open for public comment.  
 
Barbara noted that Planters Street suffers from flooding, and that the area is a mono-culture of phragmites. She 
was surprised that no abutters were present as the phragmites will probably move in and that the lack of trees 
will increase flooding.  
 
Maureen Call reiterated the previous public comment. She said they are very concerned about flooding, coastal 
storms, etc. She is concerned about trees being removed and the field being impacted.   
 
• Ms. Pearl said the area behind the trench is forested. They expect the area will revegetate. She also said the 
removal of the pipe will increase resilience of the area. There is no proposal to replace trees.  
• Mr. Hoskins said he believes trees should be replaced and that seed mix is a bare minimum. He believes the 
proposal is too passive to ensure revegetation.  
• Ms. Honora said tree planting will cause additional ground disturbance.  
• The tree removal is within the buffer zone.  
• Ms. DelNegro asked if the applicant would be willing to plant trees.  
• Photos are shared of the current conditions.  
• Mr. Ricciarelli said he believes this will have a big impact on the abutters.  
• Mr. Marcoux said even though most of the vegetation is small, they are in great abundance. Even though 
some are invasive, they are providing some flood control. Ms. Pearl said the root systems will remain intact.  
• Mr. Hoskins said a project like this typically has a planting plan.  
• Ms. Lovelace said the area is not intended to be a maintained ROW. They are hoping to do work and not 
have to come back to the property. She can talk with the applicant to about planting trees.
City of Salem Conservation Commission

Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028  
through § 2-2033. 
 
A motion to continue to the November 17th meeting was made by Lucia DelNegro, seconded by Graeme 
Marcoux, and passes 6-0. 
 
 
E. 102 Margin St- Public Hearing – Request for Determination of Applicability for Arsenio Delarosa. The 
project consists the construction of new stairs, including new footings for support. The work is located at 
102 Margin St (Map 25, Lot 644) within an area subject to protection under the Wetlands Protection Act 
and the Salem Wetlands Protection and Conservation Ordinance.  
 
Arsenio Delrosa was present representing the applicant: 
• Mr. Delrosa noted appeared before the ZBA for a change of use from a one-family to a two-family 
home. With that approval, another egress is required.  
• A rear, raised deck is proposed for the additional egress.  
• Photos of the property and the plans were shared and reviewed.  
• Excavation for four footings are required.  
• Ms. DelNegro said she had no issues with the proposal.  
• Mr. Ricciarelli noted that the area is previously disturbed.  
 
The meeting was open for public comment. There were no comments or questions.  
 
A motion to close the public hearing was made by Dayton Marchese, seconded by Dan Ricciarelli, and passes 6-0. 
 
A motion to issue a negative two and negative six determination was made by Dan Riccarelli, seconded by 
Graeme Marcoux, and passes 6-0. 
 
 
IV. OLD | NEW BUSINESS CONTINUED 
 
1.    37 March St #64-826- Request for Certificate of Compliance 
Genevieve Kavanaugh was present to discuss the request: 
• Ms. Kavanaugh said that all final documentation was provided and the site inspection with Ms. 
Vresilovic was completed.  
• Ms. Vresilovic noted that this was the seawall project that came before the Commission. She said the 
site looked good, and that they have the as-built, and letter of compliance. There is a condition on the 
order that the owner provides a status on the wall.  
• Ms. Kavanaugh said all the stones that were supposed to be cleaned up were removed.  
• There were no plantings previously on the wetland side.  
• Ms. Kavanaugh provided photos of the wall when it was under construction.  
• Mr. Marchese said the lateral drain-line photo was very helpful.  
• Ms. Vresilovic said the vote included the condition that annual inspections be conducted and that 
reports by submitted to the Commission annually by June 1st until 2031. Reports shall continue photos, 
reports on stability and any erosion that may have occurred.  
 
A motion to issue a Certificate of Compliance with the condition that ongoing annual reports on the condition of 
the wall be submitted annually to the Commission by June 1st until 2031 was made by Lucia DelNegro, seconded 
by Dayton Marchese, and passes 6-0.
City of Salem Conservation Commission 
Draft Minutes for October 22, 2026 
Page 8 of 10 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028  
through § 2-2033. 
 
 
2. 17 Strongwater Dr #64-721- Request for Partial Certificate of Compliance 
3. 19 Strongwater Dr #64-747- Request for Partial Certificate of Compliance 
4. 21 Strongwater Dr #64-741 – Request for Partial Certificate of Compliance 
Chanel DeBiase was present to discuss 17, 19, and 21 Strongwater Drive: 
• Ms. DeBiase said she met on site with Ms. Vresilovic. Partial requests for compliance were requested for 
grass establishment. She said the grass on two of the lots is doing well, but on one of lots the grass is not 
yet established.  
• Two of the homes are now owner occupied and understand that they will need to come back to the 
Commission in the spring.  
• Ms. Vresilovic said all the wetland markers have been installed. She said the erosion controls appeared 
to be in good condition.  
• Lot 21 is the lot that still has the most grass to grow.  
• Ms. DelNegro noted that some of the silt fences need support near where the wetland marker was 
installed.  She expressed concern about the amount of visible soil.  
• Ms. DeBaise said they would be willing to correct anything that needs to be addressed.  
• Ms. DeBaise said the homeowners understand that they need to come before the Commission before 
they do any work in the backyard, but she is trying to complete as many of the requirements as possible 
as the developer no longer owns the properties.  
• The HOA requires approval from any owner who wants to install a hardscape, fencing, etc. and requires 
documentation showing that they have been before the Commission.  
 
For 17 Strongwater Dr #64-721 a motion to issue a partial Certificate of Compliance was made by Graeme 
Marcous, seconded by Dan Ricciarelli, and passes 5-0, with Lucia DelNegro voting present.  
 
For 19 Strongwater Dr #64-727 a motion to issue a partial Certificate of Compliance was made by Dayton 
Marchese, seconded by Graeme Marcoux, and passes 5-0, with Lucia DelNegro voting present. 
 
For 21 Strongwater Dr #64-741 a motion to issue a partial Certificate of Compliance was made by Dan Ricciarelli, 
seconded by Graeme Marcoux, and passes 5-0, with Lucia DelNegro voting present. 
 
 
5. 15 Cleveland St #64-722- Extension Request 
• Ms. Vresilovic noted that this project had been on the September meeting agenda, which was cancelled 
due to lack of quorum. The extensive request form was filed in time for the September meeting.  
• Stephen Lovely was present to discuss the project.  
• Mr. Lovely said the project was on pause for numerous reasons, but they are hoping to get started on 
the work this Spring.  
• The extension request is for three years.  
 
A motion to grant the extension request for three years was made by Lucia DelNegro, seconded by Graeme 
Marcoux, and passes 6-0. 
 
 
6. 159 Marlborough Rd – possible violation review 
• Ms. Vresilovic said she was on site in June. She noted the backland is within the 100’ buffer zone of a 
wetland and 200’ buffer of a perennial stream. She provided a rough map showing where the wetland
City of Salem Conservation Commission 
Draft Minutes for October 22, 2026 
Page 9 of 10 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028

buffer is located.  
• During her site visit in June she did not think there were any violations. After learning that more work 
was underway, she visited the site in September and found that some work may have happened outside 
of the jurisdictional area.  
• Clearing of lower brush, dirt, and crushed stone occurred. The property owner claimed there was no 
change in grade.  
• The aerial showing the estimated wetland and buffer lines was shared and reviewed.  
• The issue came to the Commission’s attention through the City and the abutter.  
• The homeowner said the area is part of his backyard. He said the previous owner dumped quite a bit, 
and he was just cleaning it up.  
• Ms. DelNegro said the owner should have filed an NOI before doing any work within a riverfront area. 
The landowner said what he was clearing was more than 350’ away. Ms. DelNegro said the onus is on 
the landowner to prove they were outside of the buffer.  
• Ms. Vresilovic said the tree work was outside of jurisdictional area. She said within the jurisdiction it 
appeared that soil was placed within 200’ of the brook.  
• Mr. Hoskins said that the buffer lines have meaning and the Wetland Protection Act is intended to 
protect wetland and riverfront.  
• Ms. Vresilovic shared an image showing a dirt area that the landowner smoothed out.  
• Mr. Ricciarelli noted that any dirt or change in topography could impact the stream or things going into 
the stream.  
• Ms. Vresilovic said that she has heard from several abutters about this issue.  
• The landowner said he would like to clean up the property.  
• Ms. DelNegro suggested that wetland seed mix could be used.  
• Mr. Marcoux said it may make sense to get the property flagged as it will be an ongoing issue.  
• Ms. DelNegro suggested a wetland scientist be used to determine the buffer.  
• The landowner asked if he could remove some trees that may be causing a danger. Ms. Vresilovic said 
she would like to conduct another site visit and that an emergency certificate may be needed if they are 
within jurisdiction. Mr. Hoskins was supportive of that approach.

8. Forest River Conservation Area Footbridge Study funding request 
• Ms. Vresilovic noted that since the last meeting, she reached out to the City’s on-call engineers to create 
a scope of work to understand the existing conditions of the bridge, whether the pilings can be re-used,
